newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia ministers may quit in scandal - gov sources.
newsitem.headline: Colombia ministers may quit in scandal - gov sources.

text.p: BOGOTA, Aug 19 Reuter - Two top Colombian government ministers could be forced to resign at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday after being accused of illegally awarding radio broadcast licenses to friends of President Ernesto Samper, ministerial sources said.

Samper is due to convene the meeting at 1300 local time/ 1800 GMT to discuss the fate of Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar and Communications Minister Saulo Arboleda, sources at the mines and energy ministry told Reuters.
"The question of the ministers and their possible resignation will be coming up at the meeting of the council of ministers today," one of the sources told Reuters.

This week's edition of the political magazine Semana, which appeared on newsstands Monday, published parts of a recorded conversation, allegedly between Villamizar and Arboleda, in which the pair was said to have discussd how to divide up FM radio broadcast contracts among the president's friends.

The communications ministry awarded 81 new FM licenses on July 24. Villamizar and Arboleda were said to have discussed in detail how to award two radio contracts in the southwest city of Cali in the conversation said to have been taped on or about July 21.
Colombia's Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Gomez and the Attorney General Jaime Bernal both launched an investigation into the allegations that the two officials acted illegally.

The revelations in Semana led to calls for the pair to resign, while opposition Conservative Party leader Juan Camilo Restrepo said he would ask for the government ministers to be impeached in Congress.
Restrepo also questioned the process, currently under way, to award new television programming contracts.
Critics say a new television law, which obliged programmers to submit new bids for broadcast slots, is a ploy to force TV news shows that have been critical of Samper's administration off the air.
